assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: csm-build owns instruction-led execution in the current agent context and sends typed results to csm-orchestrate.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: Explicit user choice; no provider-neutral runtime is needed.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: csm-browse and csm-autoresearch use dedicated adapters because their trust boundaries differ materially.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: Browse controls CDP/session/token authority; autoresearch controls candidate/evaluator/sandbox authority.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: OpenCode removal means no OpenCode process/session/SDK fallback, not no subprocesses at all.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: All route ownership must be explicit: direct handler, csm-build handoff, browse adapter, or autoresearch adapter; BLOCKED is not complete.
Native artifacts and orchestrator references must preserve both native and shared child identities and use resolver-valid envelopes.
Generated autoresearch execution must use independently verified sandbox controls for network, mounts, credentials, resources, PIDs, descendants, and cleanup.
Every adapter must distinguish pre-dispatch cancellation from post-dispatch ambiguity and persist complete terminal/reconciliation data.
All authority checks must be tested against forged identity, digest, approval, evidence, artifact, reviewer, sandbox, and cleanup claims.

design.controlPlane: csm-orchestrate remains authoritative for route compilation, requirement ledger, approvals, identity, digests, evidence reconciliation, technical/functional gates, final review, remediation, progress, cursor/store, retries, and terminal receipt.
design.buildBoundary: csm-build exposes a current-context execution caller that consumes the child request and validated plan inputs, runs its existing lifecycle, and maps csm-build state/artifacts into csm-build-output/1 and orchestrator child references.
design.browseBoundary: A dedicated csm-browse adapter accepts only typed operations, derives owned session identity, composes CDP/session/verb APIs, translates native evidence, and owns idempotent cleanup. It never accepts arbitrary shell/CDP commands or logs tokenized URLs.
design.autoresearchBoundary: A dedicated adapter binds evaluator, candidate, policy, native run, shared child run, and artifact identities; trusted-local and generated modes have separate descriptors. Generated mode requires externally attested containment; promotion is separate human-approved work.
design.durability: Before dispatch persist complete attempt identity and intent; after handler result persist complete normalized child response and artifacts. Timeout/cancellation/crash after dispatch is UNKNOWN until reconciliation; same logical key replays only matching saved responses.
design.review: Final review receives frozen requirements/evidence without producer rationale, has distinct reviewer identity and lineage, and can insert bounded remediation that re-enters every gate.
design.observability: Every dispatch and state transition emits redacted correlated telemetry with child/native/session/trial IDs, digests, attempt, status, and reconciliation outcome.
design.release: Run the frozen baseline and expanded outcome corpus, then package closure/parity, zero-OpenCode scan, Node 22 SQLite/WAL, browser/sandbox approved gates, full repository checks, and independent final review.

executionGraph.integrationOwner: Primary build agent owns shared control-plane changes, schema registry, cross-adapter normalization, package parity, final review, and release gates.

risks: Current-context csm-build execution may not expose a callable lifecycle boundary.
CDP/session cleanup may race with browser actions or foreign processes.
Generated candidates may escape a weak sandbox or access credentials/network.
Native artifact identity may conflict with orchestrator child identity.
Durable crash windows may leave effects UNKNOWN.
Package mappings may omit transitive adapter dependencies.
mitigations: Make T001 a hard caller/coverage gate.
Use typed operation allowlists, owned session IDs, token/port/path checks, and idempotent cleanup.
Require host-attested namespaces/mount/network/resource/descendant controls for generated mode.
Preserve native and shared IDs with explicit resolver envelopes.
Persist intent and complete terminal results; reconcile before retry.
Run import closure, parity, deterministic packaging, and CI checks before release.
risksAndRecovery.rollback: Rollback the adapter commit boundary while preserving the existing no-OpenCode control-plane changes; restore explicit BLOCKED/REQUIRES_REVIEW behavior rather than a nested-session fallback.
risksAndRecovery.forwardRecovery: A missing caller, sandbox, browser host, or durable proof blocks only the affected route and keeps the all-skill release incomplete. Resume from the durable plan/checkpoint after the prerequisite is supplied.
